title: Gravity pulls without the two objects touching
summary: NASA Glenn calls gravity a field force: the source does not have to touch the object.
body: NASA Glenn's weight guide separates mechanical forces from gravity. Lift, drag, and thrust are mechanical: the object has to be in contact with the gas that makes the force. Gravity is a field force. The source does not have to be in physical contact with the object. Weight, on the same page, is the force generated by the gravitational attraction of one object on another. Page last updated 20 November 2023.

sources.title: Weight Equation
sources.author: Nancy Hall, NASA Glenn Research Center
sources.note: Public-domain NASA Glenn page, last updated 20 November 2023. Paraphrase of the field-force sentence: gravity does not require contact.
